questions: Did the eye oscillation begin suddenly in adulthood?
Has it been present since infancy or early childhood?
Do you experience your vision as moving or bouncing?
Do you have rhythmic involuntary movements of your palate or throat?
Do you have vertigo or a spinning sensation?
Do you have hearing loss or ringing in either ear?
Have you had weakness, numbness, impaired coordination, difficulty speaking, or difficulty swallowing?
Have you previously had a stroke, head injury, multiple sclerosis, or another neurological illness?
Do the eye movements continue when you close your eyes?
Are the eye movements present in only one eye?
Have you recently started or increased a medication, recreational drug, or alcohol use?
orders: Comprehensive medication, recreational-drug, and alcohol review with identification of the recently started or increased agent
Neuro-ophthalmic examination with fixation, visual acuity, ocular alignment, and cranial-nerve assessment
Video-oculography during fixation, eccentric gaze, convergence, and with fixation removed
Bedside vestibular examination, including head-impulse testing and positional testing
Serum concentration of the suspected medication, if a therapeutic drug level is available
MRI of the brain with thin-section imaging of the brainstem and cerebellum
Supervised withdrawal or dose reduction of the suspected offending medication, when clinically safe
results: 1. Comprehensive medication, recreational-drug, and alcohol review with identification of the recently started or increased agent
medication and oncology history: anti-PD-L1 durvalumab; symptoms began suddenly after the seventh administration
2. Neuro-ophthalmic examination with fixation, visual acuity, ocular alignment, and cranial-nerve assessment
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
3. Video-oculography during fixation, eccentric gaze, convergence, and with fixation removed
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: isolated pendular torsional nystagmus
4. Bedside vestibular examination, including head-impulse testing and positional testing
head impulse test: normal - no corrective saccade
5. Serum concentration of the suspected medication, if a therapeutic drug level is available
6. MRI of the brain with thin-section imaging of the brainstem and cerebellum
7. Supervised withdrawal or dose reduction of the suspected offending medication, when clinically safe
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Durvalumab-induced acquired isolated pendular torsional nystagmus (an immune-related ocular-motor adverse event)

Alternative: Durvalumab-associated autoimmune brainstem/cerebellar encephalitis causing torsional nystagmus

Alternative: MRI-negative oculopalatal tremor spectrum disorder without palatal involvement

Alternative: Paraneoplastic autoimmune ocular-motor syndrome associated with the underlying malignancy
